texts.talks:
Submission 1
Title: Lessons from usability testing at scale in production
Speaker: Umar Mensah <person-01@example.invalid>
Track: HCC track
Abstract: This talk walks through how our team approached usability testing at scale over the past year. No prior experience is needed, but familiarity with the basics helps. Expected audience: about 33 participants.

Submission 2
Title: Vector databases: what actually worked
Speaker: Pablo Fischer <person-02@example.invalid>
Track: DATA INFRA
Abstract: A hands-on look at vector databases, with code and real measurements. The session ends with a checklist attendees can apply on Monday. Expected audience: about 26 participants.

Submission 3
Title: Rethinking cost-aware warehousing
Speaker: Dara Duarte <person-03@example.invalid>
Track: data infrastructure
Abstract: We share the mistakes we made with cost-aware warehousing and how we fixed them. Expect concrete numbers, a few failure stories and an open-source companion repo. Organizers of past editions told us to plan for around 90 people.

Submission 4
Title: Long-context attention without the hype
Speaker: Dara Fischer <person-04@example.invalid>
Track: AI-Systems
Abstract: Why long-context attention is harder than it looks, and a design that holds up. The session ends with a checklist attendees can apply on Monday. Organizers of past editions told us to plan for around 24 people.

Submission 5
Title: Lessons from event sourcing in production
Speaker: Quinn Tanaka <person-05@example.invalid>
Track: Data Infrastructure
Abstract: A hands-on look at event sourcing, with code and real measurements. No prior experience is needed, but familiarity with the basics helps. Expected audience: about 43 participants.

Submission 6
Title: Notification fatigue: what actually worked
Speaker: Rosa Kowalski <person-06@example.invalid>
Track: human-centered computing
Abstract: Why notification fatigue is harder than it looks, and a design that holds up. We compare three approaches and explain the trade-offs we accepted. Expected audience: about 219 participants.

Submission 7
Title: Scaling GPU scheduling for small teams
Speaker: Hiro Iyer <person-07@example.invalid>
Track: AI systems track
Abstract: Why GPU scheduling is harder than it looks, and a design that holds up. No prior experience is needed, but familiarity with the basics helps. Organizers of past editions told us to plan for around 43 people.

Submission 8
Title: A practical guide to accessible interfaces
Speaker: Lars Silva <person-08@example.invalid>
Track: Human-Centered Computing
Abstract: Why accessible interfaces is harder than it looks, and a design that holds up. We compare three approaches and explain the trade-offs we accepted. Expected audience: about 62 participants.

Submission 9
Title: Rethinking agent tool use
Speaker: Umar Mensah <person-01@example.invalid>
Track: ai systems
Abstract: This talk walks through how our team approached agent tool use over the past year. We compare three approaches and explain the trade-offs we accepted. Expected audience: about 35 participants.

Submission 10
Title: A practical guide to retrieval-augmented generation
Speaker: Farid Kowalski <person-09@example.invalid>
Track: AI Systems
Abstract: We share the mistakes we made with retrieval-augmented generation and how we fixed them. We compare three approaches and explain the trade-offs we accepted. Organizers of past editions told us to plan for around 51 people.

Submission 11
Title: Scaling stream processing for small teams
Speaker: Rosa Kowalski <person-06@example.invalid>
Track: Data infra track
Abstract: Why stream processing is harder than it looks, and a design that holds up. The session ends with a checklist attendees can apply on Monday. We expect around 67 attendees.

Submission 12
Title: Visualizing uncertainty: what actually worked
Speaker: Dara Duarte <person-03@example.invalid>
Track: HCC track
Abstract: This talk walks through how our team approached visualizing uncertainty over the past year. Expect concrete numbers, a few failure stories and an open-source companion repo. Expected audience: about 211 participants.
